packages.name: terraform-skill
packages.prereg_row: ROADMAP M2 H2 (the staleness cost): the same skill at an older pin
packages.subtree_note: v1.0.0 has no skills/ directory: SKILL.md and references/ sit at the repo root. Only those two paths are vendored; CLAUDE.md, tests/ and CI files are not part of the skill.

staleness.kind: older pinned commit of the same upstream skill (not a bench-authored corruption)
what_is_stale: No feature-guard / version-floor table. v1.17.1 gates `removed` blocks (1.7+), provider-defined functions (1.8+), cross-variable validation (1.9+), S3 native lock-file (1.10+) and `write_only` arguments (1.11+) behind an explicit runtime floor check; v1.0.0's version guidance stops at 1.7+ and names none of them.

State locking is DynamoDB-only. v1.0.0 prescribes `dynamodb_table` (references/ci-cd-workflows.md:350, references/security-compliance.md:316) and the string `use_lockfile` appears nowhere in it; v1.17.1 says `use_lockfile` is the correct default from 1.10+ and DynamoDB is no longer required. The arms pin Terraform >= 1.11.1, so the stale advice is wrong for the runtime the agent has.
No references/state-management.md at all (v1.17.1's largest reference, 46 KB).

No schema fact-check step. v1.17.1 opens its test guidance with "validate resource schemas ... so assertions target real attributes"; the anti-hallucination guards arrived in v1.14.0 (`umbrella update ... LLM hallucination guards, fact-checks`) and are absent from v1.0.0.
staleness.why_plausibly_harmful: H2 predicts a stale skill is worse than no skill. Each item above is a concrete mechanism: confident guidance at a version floor the arm does not match (DynamoDB locking), no floor check before emitting a newer feature, and no instruction to verify an attribute name against a schema before writing it -- the last is exactly the read-before-write step whose absence the bench measures as rbw.

packages.name: aws-documentation-mcp-server
packages.prereg_row: §2.2 tuned, all arms: "AWS Docs MCP" (the deliberate fairness row)
packages.vendoring_note: Declared, not vendored: it is a server, not text. requires-python >=3.10 and six third-party dependencies (mcp, httpx, pydantic, markdownify, loguru, beautifulsoup4), so it cannot be a stdlib-only in-image file. The pinned wheel must be installed into each arm image before a tuned row is run; UNPROVEN here (no image was rebuilt).
packages.launch_form: stdio, the published console script `awslabs.aws-documentation-mcp-server` (pyproject [project.scripts] -> awslabs.aws_documentation_mcp_server.server:main). `uvx awslabs.aws-documentation-mcp-server@1.2.1`, the form the README documents, resolves from PyPI at container start: a network fetch inside the measured trial and a second uncontrolled input, so the pre-installed console script is declared instead.
packages.reaches_the_public_internet_note: This server fetches docs.aws.amazon.com at call time, by design and per prereg §2.2. It is the one tuned component whose ANSWERS the equipping hash cannot cover; the version pin bounds the client, not the corpus.

packages.name: cdk-authoring
packages.prereg_row: ROADMAP M2 H2 (the staleness cost), awscdk arm

staleness.kind: the same bench-written skill with its version-specific facts left as they were true for aws-cdk v1
what_is_stale: Package layout: `@aws-cdk/aws-<service>` per-service packages and `Construct`/`Stack` from `@aws-cdk/core`, instead of the single `aws-cdk-lib` plus the separate `constructs` package. The arm pins aws-cdk-lib 2.263.0 / constructs 10.8.1, so every import in the stale examples resolves to nothing.
Bootstrap: `CDK_NEW_BOOTSTRAP=1 cdk bootstrap` described as required. That variable was the v1 opt-in to the modern bootstrap and is meaningless in v2.
Synth: `cdk synth` without `--no-lookups`, which the arm's offline gate needs.
staleness.what_is_identical: Everything else, byte for byte: the loop, the layer table's intent, the enum guidance, the whole escape-hatch section and the Do-not list, and the frontmatter `name`/`description` -- so the level is not discoverable from inside the container.
staleness.why_plausibly_harmful: H2 predicts a stale skill is worse than no skill. A v1 import block does not compile against the arm's pinned aws-cdk-lib, so the agent spends turns recovering from confident, wrong guidance it would not have had bare; and the stale bootstrap sentence sends it at an environment step an authoring trial has no business touching.
